searchText: <@!273808422753796097> Running over lots of contracts on the blockchain with the Go profiler showed SLOAD to be far-and-away the most expensive opcode. The attached is a detailed profile of where the turbo-geth interpreter spends its time. <@!777935002263617576> You might find this helpful: https://github.com/ethereum/evmone/issues/71 Thanks, very helpful, I assume those numbers are still relevant in 2021. A few more questions: 1) Is there any comparision with https://github.com/openethereum/openethereum/tree/main/crates/vm ? Seems it's the second largest client and written in Rust, so would be interesting to know the performance. 2) Evmone exposes EVMC, however seems that major clients are lagging with EVMC support. How much battle-testing Evmone had on the mainnet? 3) Roughly how much of the time/resources are spent in EVM on the mainnet comparing to the other components such as state store management, fork choice etc. excluding PoW. <@!777935002263617576> The numbers are old enough and the clients have made enough progress that the tests need to be rerun but the overall ratios are probably the same. aleth is deprecated, geth has been improved, I'm working turbo-geth, and openethereum I didn't test. evmone is rock-solid, <@!425274498732916736> might have more to say. Pure computation is not where most clients spend their time - state access is. https://github.com/ewasm/benchmarking/tree/report According to this https://gist.github.com/chfast/d303d15d151620d23bba617cd79097af, some contracts were using up to 1MB of memory. For EVM memory: it is probably the most overpriced feature, but also memory instructions are relatively slow because they mostly compute the gas cost and check bounds or fill zeros... I strongly believe some small research of EVM memory design would be nice. page allocated memory (as in wasm) would be big improvement Thanks, very helpful! Does this include the recent geth improvements that add an on-disk state map? ah turbo-geth, I see; but surely turbo-geth would have a similar feature? anyway, this makes me really glad EIP 2929 is going live in a week Thanks <@!683653554631868440> <@!425274498732916736> , how do you run evmone in a more integerated environment (state management, consensus etc.)? https://github.com/ewasm/go-ethereum/releases seems too outdated. https://github.com/torquem-ch/silkworm Looks good, will check silkworm a bit more, but if I understand correctly it's not a full client yet? It is if combined with some turbogeth parts. I stopped updating the geth fork because there is little interest in this work

excerpts.author: gcolvin
excerpts.content: <@!273808422753796097> Running over lots of contracts on the blockchain with the Go profiler showed SLOAD to be far-and-away the most expensive opcode.  The attached is a detailed profile of where the turbo-geth interpreter spends its time.

excerpts.author: sauliusgrigaitis
excerpts.content:
Thanks, very helpful, I assume those numbers are still relevant in 2021. A few more questions:
1) Is there any comparision with https://github.com/openethereum/openethereum/tree/main/crates/vm ? Seems it's the second largest client and written in Rust, so would be interesting to know the performance.
2) Evmone exposes EVMC, however seems that major clients are lagging with EVMC support. How much battle-testing Evmone had on the mainnet?
3) Roughly how much of the time/resources are spent in EVM on the mainnet comparing to the other components such as state store management, fork choice etc. excluding PoW.

excerpts.author: gcolvin
excerpts.content: <@!777935002263617576>  The numbers are old enough and the clients have made enough progress that the tests need to be rerun but the overall ratios are probably the same.  aleth is deprecated, geth has been improved, I'm working turbo-geth, and openethereum I didn't test. evmone is rock-solid, <@!425274498732916736> might have more to say.  Pure computation is not where most clients spend their time - state access is.

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: According to this https://gist.github.com/chfast/d303d15d151620d23bba617cd79097af, some contracts were using up to 1MB of memory.

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: For EVM memory: it is probably the most overpriced feature, but also memory instructions are relatively slow because they mostly compute the gas cost and check bounds or fill zeros... I strongly believe some small research of EVM memory design would be nice.

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: page allocated memory (as in wasm) would be big improvement

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Does this include the recent geth improvements that add an on-disk state map?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: ah turbo-geth, I see; but surely turbo-geth would have a similar feature?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: anyway, this makes me really glad EIP 2929 is going live in a week
